note: Round 2. Remaining blockers: a part the opinion CONTRADICTS; a fact-bound ruling generalised into a rule; an opinion narrower than the proposition. Remaining missed positives: abstract paraphrases. One structured-criteria variant of the round-1 winner.

contradicted_part.instructions: Does `opinion` contradict or disagree with any part of `proposition`?

narrower_rule.instructions: Is the rule stated in `opinion` narrower or more limited than the rule stated in `proposition`?

fact_bound.instructions: Does `proposition` state a general legal rule that `opinion` does not state as a general rule, because the opinion only decided the question on the particular facts before it?

same_principle.instructions: Does `opinion` express the same legal principle as `proposition`, even if it uses different words?

criteria.true: The opinion expresses the whole principle in the proposition, in the same or different words
criteria.false: The opinion expresses only part of the principle, a different principle, or none

adds_specifics_structured.instructions: Does `proposition` add a specific standard, element, category, or example that does not appear in `opinion`?

criteria.true: The proposition names a test, a list of elements, a category of cases, a consequence, or a characterization that the opinion never mentions
criteria.false: Every standard, element, category, consequence, and characterization in the proposition appears in the opinion

criteria.nothing_added: Nothing: every assertion in the proposition is in the opinion
criteria.adds_detail: A clause, qualifier, detail, or stronger wording that is not in the opinion
criteria.different_point: The proposition makes a different point from the opinion

word_tracking.instructions: How closely does `opinion` track what `proposition` asserts?
criteria: The opinion is about something else
The opinion is on the same topic but does not make the assertion
The opinion makes the main assertion but not every part of it
The opinion makes every assertion in the proposition
